- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.1) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match true decline.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is neutral or weak (0.0–0.2); apply downward correction of 1–4% for 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows strong recent volatility (e.g., 3+ consecutive ±0.3 sentiment swings), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-period SMA or reduce forecast variance.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive high prices; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is flat or negative.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; force forecast to align with sentiment direction, even if price is trending down.
